name: Entrance Hall
read: Rain drums on the great doors behind you as they swing shut on a long, cold hall. A worn red carpet runs down its middle, crossed by muddy bootprints, past a toppled coat stand, a cracked mirror and a dropped lantern. On a small side table a candelabra holds candles burned down to stubs. Thunder rolls overhead, and somewhere deep in the castle a dog howls.
notes:
The great hall of Castle Varnholt. The muddy bootprints belong to the knight the village of Grausbach sent last week; they lead to the stairs in the south side. The castle is dark except where a room says otherwise.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Porter's Lodge (2, open passage), Vestibule of the Sealed Gate (3, open passage), Dining Hall (4, stairs), Specimen Gallery (5, door). The open passage in the middle of the east side leads into the Porter's Lodge, and the open passage in the middle of the west side leads into the Vestibule of the Sealed Gate. In the south side, stairs at the east end lead to the Dining Hall and a door at the west end opens into the Specimen Gallery. The double doors in the middle of the north side lead back out to the castle courtyard.

name: Porter's Lodge
read: A narrow desk and a stool stand in this small room, with an open ledger on the desk and a rack of old iron keys on the wall above it. Coils of copper wire run along the walls and down into the floor, where square copper plates are set among the flagstones. The air smells sharp, like the air after a lightning strike.
notes:
The castle porter once kept the door from here. Varnholt dismissed his servants long ago and wired the floor against intruders. The ledger lists the graves of the Grausbach churchyard he has opened, with names and dates, ten years of them. The keys on the rack are old and open nothing of importance.

Trap: Galvanic Floor

  • Trigger: a creature steps onto the copper plates in the middle of the floor.
  • Find: DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) notices that the wires run down into the copper plates, and a faint blue spark jumping between two of them.
  • Effect: DC 16 Constitution saving throw [[/save con 16]]; [[/damage 10d10 lightning]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure the creature also has the Prone condition.
  • Disarm or avoid: Cut the wires where they leave the wall (DC 15 Dexterity check with thieves' tools or tinker's tools), or walk along the walls, where there are no plates.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: a Galvanic Lantern on the desk beside the ledger.

Exits: Entrance Hall (1, open passage), Dining Hall (4, door). The open passage in the middle of the west side leads into the Entrance Hall. The door at the west end of the south side opens into the Dining Hall.

name: Vestibule of the Sealed Gate
read: This small stone room is bare except for two stone benches and a dusty rug. Set into the south wall is a round gate of solid stone, carved all over with feathers, with a keyhole in the shape of a bird at its centre. A wooden door stands in the west wall.
notes:
The round stone gate is the old gate of the Varnholt family, whose crest is a raven. It is locked. The Bird-Shaped Key from the Plundered Crypt (room 11) opens it. The lock can also be picked (DC 18 Dexterity check with thieves' tools) or the gate forced open (DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check). Beyond it lies the Specimen Gallery.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Entrance Hall (1, open passage), Library (6, door), Specimen Gallery (5, locked round stone gate). The open passage in the middle of the east side leads into the Entrance Hall. The door at the north end of the west side opens into the Library. The locked round stone gate in the south side opens into the Specimen Gallery.

name: Dining Hall
read: A long table runs the length of this hall, laid for a feast that has rotted where it stands: grey meat, black fruit and wine gone sour in the glasses. Chairs lie overturned, broken plates cover the floor, and a great chandelier has fallen and cracked in the middle of the room. Among the gnawed bones under the table, something is breathing.
notes:
Every year on the day of his wedding, Varnholt lays this feast for two and sits at it alone. Nobody eats it. The place at the head of the table is set for Elsa. The hounds from the Kennels (room 7) feed on the scraps.

Encounter (Power Level 8, Durability 15)

Five Stitched Hounds lie under the table among the bones. They rise and attack when a creature enters the hall, and fight until destroyed.

Treasure: a Potion of Healing in a silver tureen at Elsa's place at the head of the table.

Exits: Entrance Hall (1, stairs), Porter's Lodge (2, door), Burned Gallery (8, door and stairs). In the north side, stairs at the west end lead to the Entrance Hall and a door in the middle opens into the Porter's Lodge. A door in the south side, east of the middle, opens onto a short passage south that ends in stairs down to the north side of the Burned Gallery.

name: Specimen Gallery
read: Rows of glass jars on low stands fill this long gallery, each full of glowing green fluid in which pale things float: hands, eyes, and a curled shape with too many fingers. A brass label is fixed to every stand, and a few jars lie smashed in puddles on the floor. At the far end, four tall figures in leather aprons stand perfectly still, copper bolts glinting at their necks.
notes:
Varnholt keeps the best parts from the Grausbach churchyard here. Each brass label gives the name of the villager the part came from. The fluid in the jars gives a dim blue-green light across the gallery.

Encounter (Power Level 10, Durability 16)

Four Galvanic Servants stand guard at the west end. They wake when a creature enters, and fight until destroyed. Lightning chains between servants that stand close together, as their stat block describes.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Entrance Hall (1, door), Vestibule of the Sealed Gate (3, locked round stone gate), Kennels (7, door). In the north side, a door at the east end opens into the Entrance Hall and the locked round stone gate in the middle opens into the Vestibule of the Sealed Gate. The gate is locked from both sides; see room 3. The door at the north end of the west side opens into the Kennels.

name: Library
read: Shelves of books climb every wall of this library, and more books stand in tall piles on the floor. A reading desk holds open books of anatomy and drawings of the human body, crossed with arrows and marks like lightning. Beside an armchair, two glass jars on wheeled stands each hold a grey brain in cloudy fluid, and both jars turn toward you.
notes:
Varnholt's study. The two brains belonged to the old schoolmaster and the old priest of Grausbach; Varnholt keeps them to read to him and to keep his notes in order. His notes on restarting dead flesh with lightning are here, ten years of them.

Encounter (Power Level 11, Durability 18)

Two Brain in a Jar constructs and two Stitched Hounds. The hounds lie beside the armchair and attack first. The brains roll back behind them and throw books and furniture with their minds. They fight until destroyed.

Treasure: Goggles of Night in the drawer of the reading desk.

Exits: Vestibule of the Sealed Gate (3, door), Kennels (7, archway), Generator Hall (9, door and open passage). The door at the south end of the east side opens into the Vestibule of the Sealed Gate. The archway in the middle of the south side leads into the Kennels. A door at the south end of the west side opens onto a passage west that opens into the middle of the east side of the Generator Hall.

name: Kennels
read: Iron cages line this long room, and every cage door hangs open. Chains with empty collars trail from the walls through dirty straw, among gnawed bones, water bowls and torn leather muzzles. The smell of wet dog and old blood is very strong.
notes:
The Stitched Hounds were kept here. Tonight Varnholt let them all loose to guard the castle, and they now lie in the Dining Hall (room 4) and the Library (room 6).

No encounter.

Treasure: a Potion of Climbing in the pocket of a keeper's coat hanging on a peg by the door.

Exits: Library (6, archway), Specimen Gallery (5, door). The archway at the east end of the north side leads into the Library. The door in the middle of the east side opens into the Specimen Gallery.

name: Burned Gallery
read: Portraits of a stern family once hung along these walls; most now lie face down on the charred floorboards. On an easel at one end stands a great gilded frame, but the painting inside it has burned to a black crust, with only a scrap of painted white lace left in one corner. Ash lies thick on the floor around it.
notes:
The portrait was Elsa's. Emeric burned it on the night he found he could no longer remember her face. His grief has kept the fire alive in the frame.

Trap: Burning Portrait

  • Trigger: a creature comes within 5 feet of the easel or touches the frame.
  • Find: DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) notices that the ash around the easel is warm, and that the cracks in the black crust glow faintly red.
  • Effect: DC 15 Dexterity saving throw [[/save dex 15]]; [[/damage 10d10 fire]] on a failure, half on a success.
  • Disarm or avoid: Pour water or any other liquid over the frame from at least 10 feet away, or keep more than 5 feet from the easel.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: a Hat of Disguise — a plain black opera hat left on the easel beside the burned portrait.

Exits: Dining Hall (4, stairs and door), Morgue (10, door), Plundered Crypt (11, stairs). Stairs in the middle of the north side climb to a short passage that ends at a door into the Dining Hall. The door at the north end of the west side opens into the Morgue. Stairs at the north end of the east side lead down to the Plundered Crypt.

name: Generator Hall
read: A great sphere of glass hangs in the air in the middle of this hall, full of blue lightning that burns and crackles against the glass. Beneath it a ring of copper coils hums, and thick cables run across the floor to levers, gauges and brass batteries along the walls. A gaunt man in a stained surgeon's coat works the levers, with two tall figures in leather aprons beside him. In the north wall, stairs climb into the dark.
notes:
The burning sphere stores the lightning of the storm and sends it up the stairs to the Tower Laboratory (room 12). It gives blue light across the hall. The man is Dr. Emeric Varnholt, making the last adjustments before he wakes the Bride.

Encounter (Power Level 11, Durability 16.5)

Dr. Emeric Varnholt and two Galvanic Servants. Varnholt is an Epic commander: he gives orders to the servants and fights from behind them. He does not ask for mercy, and he does not offer it. The first time he drops to 0 Hit Points while the Bride lives, he drops to 1 Hit Point instead and flees up the stairs to her; he joins the fight in room 12.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Library (6, open passage and door), Tower Laboratory (12, stairs). The open passage in the middle of the east side leads to a passage east that ends at a door into the Library. Stairs in the middle of the north side climb to the Tower Laboratory.

name: Morgue
read: Stone slabs stand in rows in this cold room, each holding a shape under a stained sheet, with a drain in the floor between them. A cart beside the door holds saws and hooks, and buckets stand beneath the slabs. Toe tags hang from the bare feet that stick out from under the sheets, and on some slabs the two feet are not the same size.
notes:
Varnholt keeps the bodies from the Grausbach churchyard here until he needs them. The toe tags give the names of the village dead. The largest shape, under a sheet the size of a sail, is the finished Patchwork Horror.

Encounter (Power Level 9, Epic Boss, Durability 13.5)

One Patchwork Horror, an Epic Boss sewn from many of the village dead, lies under the great sheet. It rises when a creature reaches the middle of the room and fights until destroyed. It acts on initiative count 10 and takes one Response after each character's turn. When Bloodied its seams split and grasping parts reach out around it; when it drops to 0 Hit Points it comes apart, as its stat block describes.

Treasure: a Potion of Healing on the cart among the saws.

Exits: Burned Gallery (8, door), Operating Theatre (13, door). The door in the middle of the east side opens into the Burned Gallery. The door in the south side, west of the middle, opens into the Operating Theatre.

name: Plundered Crypt
read: Two stone coffins stand open in this low crypt, their lids pushed aside and their bones gone. A dug-up grave marker leans against the wall beside bottles of embalming fluid and a copper pump with a long hose. On the floor slumps a knight in dented armour, his face blue, his hand closed around something that glints.
notes:
The crypt of the Varnholt family; Emeric took the bones of his own ancestors first. The knight is Sir Benedikt Kohl, sent by the village of Grausbach last week. He found the Bird-Shaped Key in the coffin of the first lord of the castle, and the embalming gas killed him where he stood.

Trap: Embalming Gas

  • Trigger: a creature touches the knight or either coffin, or steps between the coffins.
  • Find: DC 16 Intelligence (Investigation) notices that the hose of the copper pump runs into small holes in the floor between the coffins, and a sharp chemical smell.
  • Effect: DC 15 Constitution saving throw [[/save con 15]]; [[/damage 10d10 poison]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure the creature also has the Poisoned condition for 1 hour.
  • Disarm or avoid: Close the valve on the copper pump (an action, once the hose is found), or stuff the holes in the floor with cloth.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: the Bird-Shaped Key (story item; it opens the locked round stone gate between the Vestibule of the Sealed Gate and the Specimen Gallery) in the knight's hand.

Exits: Burned Gallery (8, stairs). Stairs in the middle of the west side climb to the Burned Gallery.

name: Tower Laboratory
read: An iron operating table stands raised in the middle of this tower room, and on it, under leather straps, lies a tall woman stitched together from many bodies, a veil of white lace over her face. Beside the table a copper coil taller than a man throws lightning up through a hole in the roof, and cables tangle across chalk diagrams drawn on the floor. Two tall figures in leather aprons stand at the straps. The coil roars, and the woman's hand closes into a fist.
notes:
The end of the adventure. The woman is The Bride: a body Varnholt built from the dead of Grausbach to hold his wife Elsa. The veil is cut from Elsa's wedding dress. The coil draws the storm down onto the castle and gives pale blue light across the room. At its core is The Galvanic Heart.

Encounter (Power Level 12, Durability 18)

The Bride and two Galvanic Servants. The Bride is an Epic Boss: she never rolls initiative, acts on initiative count 10, and takes one Response after each player character's turn. If Varnholt fled here from the Generator Hall, he stands at the coil with 1 Hit Point and works its levers.

The coil. While the coil runs, the Bride grows stronger: at initiative count 10 each round she regains 20 Hit Points, and her attacks deal an extra 1d10 lightning damage for each round of the fight so far, to a maximum of 4d10. A creature can wreck the coil by dealing it 60 damage (AC 18), or by using an action and succeeding on a DC 20 Strength (Athletics) or Intelligence (Arcana) check. When the coil is wrecked, the Bride stops growing stronger and loses her Epic Boss Resistance for the rest of the fight.

Coil arcs. Lightning leaps between the two tower coils and down to the generator. A creature that enters or starts its turn within 10 feet of the arcs makes a DC 19 Constitution saving throw, taking 18 (2d8 + 9) Lightning damage on a failure or half as much on a success; creatures immune to lightning are unharmed. If the Bride enters or starts her turn there, she regains 20 Hit Points instead. The arcs are automated (Monk's Active Tiles). When the coil is wrecked, the GM clicks the lightning icon outside the east wall of the room to shut the arcs, their animation and the room's blue light off; click it again to restart them.

The Galvanic Heart. Once the coil is wrecked or the Bride is dead, a creature can pull the Heart free as an action. When the Heart leaves the coil, the storm loses its hold on the castle and breaks before dawn.

Treasure: The Galvanic Heart (story item; the core of the coil that powers the Bride), an Amulet of Health around the Bride's neck, and 600 gp in a small pile under the table.

Exits: Generator Hall (9, stairs). Stairs in the middle of the south side lead down to the Generator Hall.

name: Operating Theatre
read: A surgical lamp on a tall stand throws hard white light over an iron operating table in the middle of this room. Trays of knives, saws and needles stand beside it, among bloody cloths and jars of organs. A grey brain in a glass jar on a wheeled stand turns slowly to face you, and large shapes rise from the shadows along the walls.
notes:
Varnholt built his Patchwork Horror here. The lamp gives bright white light around the table. The brain is that of the old village doctor of Grausbach, Varnholt's teacher, who now assists him.

Encounter (Power Level 11, Durability 18)

One Brain in a Jar and three Galvanic Servants. The Servants stand along the walls and spread out so their lightning crosses the room; the Brain stays behind the operating table and throws trays and tools with its mind. They fight until destroyed.

Treasure: a Potion of Healing on a tray of tools, and a pair of Eyes of Minute Seeing (Varnholt's surgical lenses) on the lamp stand.

Exits: Morgue (10, door), Lady Varnholt's Chamber (14, barred iron door), Holding Cells (15, stairs). The door in the middle of the north side opens into the Morgue. The barred iron door near the north end of the east side opens into Lady Varnholt's Chamber; see room 14 for its brass knob. Stairs near the north end of the west side lead down to the Holding Cells.

name: Lady Varnholt's Chamber
read: This bedchamber is kept as if its lady had only just stepped out: the four-poster bed is made, fresh candles burn, and dried flowers fill every vase. A dressing table holds a mirror, a hairbrush and a jewelry box. Above it hangs a wedding portrait in which the bride's face has worn away to a pale blur, as if rubbed by a thumb many times. There is no dust anywhere.
notes:
Elsa's room, where she died of fever ten years ago. Emeric cleans it himself every day.

The barred door. The barred iron door from the Operating Theatre has a brass knob. Its bar lifts without a check. The first time a creature touches the knob, read:

The iron is warm under your hand, and the room beyond it is suddenly bright with morning. A young woman with dark hair lies in the four-poster bed, pale and burning with fever. A younger man sits beside her in a clean coat, holding her wrist and counting her pulse aloud, and the count grows slower, and stops. He does not let go of her hand. For a long time he sits without moving, and then he says to the empty room, very quietly: I will not lose you. I will bring you back, if I have to pull the lightning out of the sky. The light goes out, and the knob is cold.

No encounter.

Treasure: Elsa's Locket in the jewelry box, holding a lock of dark hair, and 500 gp in her dowry box under the bed.

Exits: Operating Theatre (13, barred iron door). The barred iron door in the middle of the west side opens into the Operating Theatre.

name: Holding Cells
read: Iron cell doors line the walls of this low room, most of them standing open on bare cells. In the middle of the floor a heavy iron cage hangs from a chain just above a straw pallet, with manacles and a bucket beside it. A wooden chest sits against the far wall.
notes:
Varnholt kept the grave diggers he hired here once they knew too much. The cells are empty now. The chest holds what he took from them.

Trap: Restraint Cage

  • Trigger: a creature steps onto the straw pallet under the hanging cage, on the straight way to the chest.
  • Find: DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) notices that the chain runs up to a release catch in the ceiling, and deep scrapes in the floor where the cage has fallen before.
  • Effect: DC 16 Strength saving throw [[/save str 16]]; [[/damage 10d10 bludgeoning]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure the creature also has the Restrained condition, held by the cage clamps until it or an ally uses an action and succeeds on a DC 16 Strength (Athletics) check.
  • Disarm or avoid: Wedge the release catch (DC 16 Dexterity check with thieves' tools), or walk around the pallet along the walls.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: 300 gp in the chest, with rations and a suit of ordinary scale mail.

Exits: Operating Theatre (13, stairs). Stairs in the middle of the east side climb to the Operating Theatre.
